working_title: Scotland's Angus Links: A Practical Guide to Playing Carnoustie, Panmure, Monifieth and Montrose
angle: Angus is far more than one famous name on an Open rota. This post makes the case for treating the tight coastal strip between Carnoustie and Montrose as a self-contained golf circuit, showing how a visiting UK golfer can string together several days of authentic, varied links golf without straying far from a single base.
research_notes:
- Angus region has around 30 golf courses, with a cluster of links courses sitting close together along the North Sea coast (Carnoustie, Panmure, Monifieth, Montrose).
- Carnoustie Golf Links is publicly accessible and offers three courses: the Championship Course, the Burnside Course, and the Buddon Course. Championship tee times are in high demand in peak season and should be booked well ahead (several months for summer dates); online booking or phone via Carnoustie Golf Links directly.
- The Championship Course has hosted eight Open Championships and is known colloquially as 'Carnasty' for its difficulty: 112 bunkers, the Barry Burn crossing the 17th and 18th, and a demanding finishing stretch. The course is strategic rather than scenic in the postcard sense.
- Burnside and Buddon courses offer more accessible (and lower green-fee) alternatives on the same site.
- Panmure Golf Club sits just along the coast from Carnoustie and is described as an understated inland links. Historically notable as where Ben Hogan practised before his 1953 Open win at Carnoustie.
- Monifieth Golf Links is also within a few miles and provides another traditional east-coast links option.
- Montrose Golf Links: one of the oldest golf venues in the world, with recorded play dating to 1562, making it the fifth oldest course in the world. Offers two courses: the 1562 Course (Medal/Championship) and the shorter Broomfield Course. Located around 20 miles north of Carnoustie (approx. 30 minutes). Visitors welcome.
- The whole circuit is roughly 30 minutes end-to-end, making 36-hole days and multi-course trips very practical.
- Carnoustie town is around 11 miles from Dundee and 90 minutes by car from Edinburgh. Dundee provides more hotel and restaurant choice; Carnoustie town itself is practical but modest. Staying in Carnoustie gives walk-to-the-first-tee convenience.
- Stonehaven Golf Club (Aberdeenshire, 15 miles south of Aberdeen) is an option for those extending the circuit northward toward Aberdeen.
- Royal Aberdeen (Balgownie) and Cruden Bay (23 miles north of Aberdeen) are Aberdeenshire highlights for those extending the trip further north, but are a different leg of the journey.
- Trump International Scotland (Menie Estate, 16km north of Aberdeen) opened a New Course in July 2025 alongside the existing Hawtree-designed Old Course.
- Edzell Golf Club lies inland at the gateway to the Angus Glens and offers heathland variety as a change of pace from the coastal courses.
- No specific green fee figures should be used for 2026 as the research notes contain outdated or unverified prices; describe costs in general terms only.
